title: A-gei (Taiwanese fried tofu stuffed with glass noodles)
steps: Stir-fry the pork or mushrooms briefly with soy sauce, then toss in the soaked glass noodles until they absorb the flavours.
Cut a small opening in each tofu pouch and fill with the noodle mixture.
Seal the opening with fish paste, smoothing it.
Steam the pouches for 10 minutes, or simmer in stock until firm.
Serve with sweet chili sauce.

title: Aiyu jelly (Taiwanese fig seed jelly with lemon)
steps: Put the aiyu seeds in a muslin bag, submerge them in the water and knead for 5 to 10 minutes until the water turns slippery and cloudy.
Squeeze the bag out well and discard the seeds.
Let the liquid sit for an hour or so in a bowl until it sets into a soft jelly.
Make a syrup by dissolving the sugar in a little hot water with lemon juice, and chill.
Spoon the jelly into bowls, add ice and syrup, and serve cold.

title: Ba-wan (Taiwanese meatball in a translucent starch skin)

ingredients.name: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and chopped

ingredients.measure: sweet chili or garlic soy sauce
ingredients.name: to serve

steps: Mix the pork with the mushrooms, bamboo shoots, soy sauce, pepper and sesame oil and shape into 8 balls.
Stir both starches with a pinch of salt, then pour in the boiling water and mix to a sticky, translucent dough.
Wrap a thick layer of dough around each filling ball, using oiled hands, and place each on an oiled square of baking paper.
Steam over high heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the skins are clear and glossy.
Cool slightly and serve with sweet chili sauce or garlic soy sauce.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chiayi turkey rice (Taiwanese shredded turkey over rice)
steps: Poach the turkey in simmering salted water for 25 to 35 minutes until just cooked through, then cool and shred it by hand, saving some broth.
Fry the shallots in the oil until golden and crisp, and take them out, leaving the fragrant oil.
Mix the shallot oil with the soy sauce, sugar and broth and simmer for a few minutes into a light gravy.
Mound the rice into bowls, pile on the shredded turkey and pour the gravy over.
Top with crispy shallots and pickled radish.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Coffin bread (Taiwanese fried bread filled with creamy stew)

ingredients.name: thick slices of white bread (about 5 cm)

steps: Melt the butter, add the chicken and cook until it turns white, then stir in the flour.
Whisk in the milk and add the carrot and peas, simmering until thick, and season well.
Cut a lid from the top of each bread slice and hollow out the centre.
Deep-fry the bread boxes and lids at 170°C until golden brown, about 2 minutes.
Fill the boxes with the hot filling, put on the lids and serve at once.

title: Cuttlefish geng (Taiwanese thick cuttlefish soup)

ingredients.name: white fish paste or minced fish

steps: Cut the cuttlefish into strips and toss with some starch.
Mix the fish paste with a little salt and starch and coat the cuttlefish with it, making thick strips.
Bring the stock to a boil with the carrot and the soy sauce and thicken with a starch slurry.
Slide in the coated cuttlefish and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.
Season with pepper and finish with basil, black vinegar and sesame oil.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Danbing (Taiwanese egg crepe breakfast)

ingredients.measure: soy paste or sweet chili sauce
ingredients.name: to serve

steps: Whisk the flour, starch, water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and rest 15 minutes.
Brush a flat non-stick pan with oil and pour in a quarter of the batter, spreading it thin.
When the crepe is almost set, crack an egg onto it, break the yolk and spread with the spoon.
Scatter spring onions and cheese or ham over it, then flip once to briefly set the egg.
Roll up the crepe, cut it into pieces and serve with soy paste or chili sauce.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Danzai noodles (Tainan noodles with shrimp broth and pork)
steps: Fry the shallots in oil until golden, add the pork and cook until browned.
Add the soy sauce, wine, sugar and 200 ml of water and simmer for 30 minutes until rich and saucy.
Simmer the shrimp heads and shells in the remaining water for 25 minutes, then strain to make a shrimp broth.
Poach the peeled shrimp briefly in the broth, then lift them out.
Blanch the noodles for 30 seconds and divide among small bowls.
Add hot broth, a spoonful of pork sauce, a shrimp and the garlic chives, with a splash of black vinegar.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Eel noodles (Taiwanese tainan sweet and sour eel noodles)

ingredients.name: yi mein noodles or fresh wheat noodles

steps: Coat the eel in a little starch and fry it in 2 tablespoons of oil until browned.
Fry the garlic and green pepper in the remaining oil, add the stock, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar and bring to a simmer.
Thicken with a starch slurry until slightly glossy.
Return the eel to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes.
Cook the noodles, divide among bowls, pour the sauce over and add garlic chives.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Gua bao (Taiwanese steamed pork belly buns)

ingredients.name: crushed roasted peanuts, mixed with sugar

steps: Brown the pork slab lightly in a dry pot, then add the soy sauce, wine, sugar, star anise, ginger and water.
Simmer, covered, for 1.5 hours until the pork is tender, turning occasionally.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, then slice it into thick pieces.
Steam the buns for 8 to 10 minutes until puffy.
Open each bun and fill with a slice of pork, a spoonful of braising liquid, pickled greens, peanut-sugar and coriander.
Serve the buns warm, with extra braising liquid on the side.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Ji pai (Taiwanese giant fried chicken cutlet)
steps: Slice the breasts in half horizontally and pound them thin and wide with a mallet.
Marinate in the soy sauce, wine, garlic, five-spice and pepper for 30 minutes, then mix in the egg.
Press each cutlet firmly into the starch, coating both sides, and rest 5 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry each cutlet for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with chili powder and salt, and cut into strips.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kong rou fan (Taiwanese braised pork belly rice)

ingredients.name: pork belly in one piece, cut into 3 cm chunks

steps: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Place it in a heavy pot with the soy sauces, wine, sugar, star anise, ginger and spring onions.
Add the water to cover, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until fork-tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for 10 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Serve the pork on rice with plenty of sauce spooned over, and greens on the side.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Lu rou fan (Taiwanese minced pork rice)
steps: Fry the shallots in the oil over medium-low heat until deep golden and crisp, then lift out half and keep for topping.
Add the pork to the pot and cook until it loses its raw colour and some fat renders.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauces, sugar and five-spice and stir for a minute.
Add the water and the eggs, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 to 1.5 hours until the pork is soft and the sauce glossy.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, thinning with a little water if the sauce reduces too far.
Ladle over bowls of hot rice with an egg half and the reserved shallots, and serve with something pickled.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Milkfish congee (Taiwanese tilapia or milkfish rice porridge)

ingredients.name: milkfish belly or white fish fillets

steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with the water in a covered pot at a gentle simmer for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and thick.
Slice the fish into thin pieces and mix with the soy sauce, wine and ginger.
Season the congee with salt and pepper.
Add the fish to the simmering congee and cook for 2 minutes until just opaque.
Serve in bowls topped with spring onions and fried shallots.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Moon shrimp cake (Taiwanese pan-fried shrimp rounds)
steps: Mix the shrimp, pork fat, water chestnuts, ginger, fish sauce, sesame oil and pepper into a sticky paste.
Spread the paste in a thin even layer over half of the wrappers, then cover with another wrapper to make a sandwich.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the rounds over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with sweet chili sauce.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Oyster omelette (Taiwanese o-a-tsian)

ingredients.name: sweet and mild chili sauce (ketchup, sugar, a little soy and starch)

steps: Rinse the oysters in cold salted water, drain and pat dry.
Whisk the starch with the water into a thin slurry.
Heat the oil in a wide non-stick pan and sear the oysters for 1 minute with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Stir the starch slurry again, pour it over the oysters and cook until it turns translucent and sticky.
Pour in the beaten eggs and let it set, then add the greens on top.
Flip or fold the omelette, let it crisp lightly and slide onto a plate, topping with the sweet-savoury sauce.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Oyster vermicelli (Taiwanese oyster and mian xian thick soup)

ingredients.name: sweet potato starch, mixed with 3 tbsp water

steps: Rinse the oysters gently in salted water, drain and toss them in a little starch.
Bring the stock to a boil with the soy sauce and sugar.
Stir in the starch slurry and simmer until the soup is lightly thick.
Add the oysters and cook 1 to 2 minutes until just firm.
Add the vermicelli and heat through.
Ladle into bowls and top with garlic, coriander, black vinegar and sesame oil.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Peanut ice cream roll (Taiwanese popiah-style ice cream wrap)

ingredients.name: thin popiah or spring-roll wrappers (or crepes)
peanut brittle, shaved or finely crushed

steps: Lay the wrappers flat on a board.
Sprinkle a thick layer of shaved peanut brittle over each wrapper.
Add two scoops of ice cream in a line and the coriander.
Fold in the two sides, roll up tightly and eat right away before the ice cream melts.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Pineapple cake (Taiwanese pineapple shortbread)
steps: Cook the pineapple with the sugar and maltose over medium heat, stirring, until a thick sticky jam remains, about 35 minutes, then cool completely and roll into 20 g balls.
Rub the butter into the flour, milk powder, icing sugar and salt, then add the egg yolk and mix into a soft dough.
Chill the dough for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into pieces about 25 g each, flatten each, wrap around a ball of filling and press into a small mould or shape into a rectangle.
Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes, flip, and bake another 10 minutes until golden.
Cool on a rack before eating.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Pineapple shrimp balls (Taiwanese fried shrimp with pineapple)
steps: Chop the shrimp roughly and mix with the egg white, cornstarch, salt and pepper.
Press a handful around each pineapple chunk to make a ball.
Roll the balls in breadcrumbs, pressing so they stick.
Fry at 170°C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, in small batches.
Drain and serve with mayonnaise for dipping.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sanbeiji (Taiwanese three-cup chicken)

ingredients.name: chicken thighs on the bone, chopped into pieces

steps: Heat the sesame oil in a clay pot or heavy pan over medium heat and fry the ginger slices until curling at the edges.
Add the garlic and chilies and cook until the garlic is golden.
Add the chicken and sear for about 5 minutes, turning, until browned.
Pour in the soy sauce, wine and sugar, cover and cook on medium-low for 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is nearly gone.
Uncover, boil down any extra liquid until sticky, stir in the basil and take off the heat. Serve with rice.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Taiwanese beef noodle soup (red-braised beef noodle soup)

ingredients.name: beef shank, cut into big chunks

ingredients.measure: pickled mustard greens, chopped spring onion
ingredients.name: to serve

steps: Blanch the beef in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Fry the doubanjiang in the oil for 1 to 2 minutes, add the ginger, garlic and spring onions and stir until fragrant.
Add the beef, then the soy sauce, wine, sugar, spices and tomatoes and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours until the beef is very tender.
Lift out the beef and slice it, keeping the broth hot and seasoning it to taste.
Boil the noodles and bok choy separately, divide into bowls, add the beef and ladle over the broth, finishing with pickled greens and spring onion.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Taiwanese fried chicken (popcorn chicken with crispy basil)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into small pieces
salt mixed with 1/2 tsp white pepper

steps: Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, wine, garlic, five-spice and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Stir in the egg, then toss the chicken in the sweet potato starch, pressing it on, and rest for 5 minutes so the coating becomes damp.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden.
Raise the heat, return all the chicken to the oil for 30 seconds to crisp.
Fry the basil leaves for about 10 seconds until crisp, and drain with the chicken.
Toss together with the salt and pepper mix and serve right away.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Tsang Ying Tou (stir-fried garlic chives with pork and black beans)

ingredients.name: garlic chives, cut into 2 cm pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a wok and brown the pork over high heat, breaking up lumps.
Add the garlic, chilies and black beans and stir for 1 minute.
Splash in the wine and soy sauce, then add the sugar.
Add the garlic chives and toss for 1 to 2 minutes only so they stay bright and crisp.
Serve with rice.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Tsua-ping (Taiwanese shaved ice with sweet toppings)

ingredients.name: cooked taro or sweet potato cubes
cooked peanuts or grass jelly cubes

steps: Prepare the toppings and keep them cool.
Shave the ice into a fine snowy pile, using a shaver or a blender with short pulses.
Divide the ice between bowls and pile the beans, taro, peanuts or grass jelly over and around it.
Drizzle with the brown sugar syrup and condensed milk.
Serve immediately before it melts.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Tube rice pudding (Taiwanese bamboo-tube glutinous rice)

ingredients.name: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and chopped
bamboo tubes or small heat-proof cups

steps: Stir-fry the pork, mushrooms and dried shrimp in the oil until fragrant, seasoning with soy sauce and pepper.
Add the drained rice and stir-fry briefly so it absorbs the flavour.
Pack the mixture into the bamboo tubes or small cups, leaving some room at the top.
Steam over high heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the rice is sticky and cooked through.
Push the rice out of the tubes and slice, or serve in the cups.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Wheel pie (Taiwanese hui lun bing sweet pancake cakes)
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the milk and oil.
Stir in the flour and baking powder to make a smooth batter and rest for 20 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled round mould or egg-ring in a pan and fill half with batter.
Add a spoonful of bean paste, then cover with a little more batter.
Cook over low heat for about 3 minutes, flip and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve the cakes warm, straight from the pan.
